pull.title: feat(deadlines): ship every deadline at 0, and name the knob in the error
pull.body:
## What was wrong

The five deadline defaults — 180 s first token, 600 s total budget, 180 s share floor, 180 s stall, 450 s thinking — were measured off 21 days of this project's own traffic and were correct for that traffic. They were wrong for a reasoning model that legitimately thinks for half an hour, and the failure they caused was the expensive one: a model doing real work killed mid-thought.

The error the client then received said `Provider 'x' produced only reasoning for 450s without answering.` True, and useless. The reader's next question is always "where do I change that?", and the answer was three files and a search away — which in practice meant the number stayed as it was.

## What changed

**All five deadlines ship at `0` — no limit.** With the shipped zeros MCC never ends a silent or stalled upstream on its own; the fallback chain moves only on an error the provider returns. That is the deliberate position: this is a server its operator configures, so the shipped value is the one that decides nothing. It is now stated plainly in one place each in `README.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, the Deadlines card blurb and the in-dashboard Guide, together with what each limit measures and how to get time-based failover back (`FALLBACK_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT` is the only one that produces a *failover*; the others end the request). **An install that already sets any of the five keys keeps its own value.**

**Every limit now names its own knob in the error.** New `application/deadline_hints.py` appends ` (<ENV_VAR> -- change it on the dashboard under Limits & Resilience -> <Card>)`. The card label is read out of the admin manifest's own `SECTIONS`, and a contract test pins the page name against the nav label in `admin.js`, so the words cannot drift from the page they point at. Applied at the five deadline messages, the stepped-over cooldown verdict, and the one `All API keys for this provider are in cooldown` string in `providers/runtime/rotating.py`.

The hint names the limit that **actually** ended the attempt: a silent model cut short by its slice of the request budget names `FALLBACK_ATTEMPT_SHARE_FLOOR`, not the first-token box that never fired. ASCII throughout, because this text crosses an SSE frame, a JSON body, a request-log row and a terminal.

## Scope

Constants, strings, docs and tests. **No deadline, retry, rotation or fallback logic changed.** Every `> 0` guard in `_chunk_timeout` / `_attempt_deadline` already treated 0 as disabled and `LIMIT_RANGES` already admitted 0, so a zero default needed no code path of its own. `_timeout_env_var` reads the decision `_deadline_reached` had already made; `share_bound` is a boolean that picks a string. `providers/credential_rotation.py`, `core/credential_rotation.py` and `providers/rate_limit.py` are untouched, and `rotating.py` changed by exactly one error string plus its import.

The 6.15.0 committed-stream truncation path records the same `ExecutionFailure` rather than raising it, so the hint on `stopped producing output for Ns` reaches the attempt row there too — one helper, both paths.

## Verification

**Real executor, shipped policy, four silent fake models.** `test_the_shipped_policy_never_ends_a_silent_model_itself`: the request is still running after 1.5 s and only the first model was ever reached — the chain has no reason to advance, because nothing returned an error. `test_one_deadline_set_is_enough_to_get_the_failover_back` sets one knob and the same four models are all walked, ending with the hint.

**Live, isolated server on `127.0.0.1:8199`** with `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` redirected to a scratch home (8082 and `~/.fcc` untouched; `netstat` checked before and after), against a local upstream that accepts the request and then produces nothing. With `FALLBACK_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT=5`, both streaming and non-streaming returned HTTP 504 and this exact body:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"timeout_error","message":"Provider 'custom_fake/fake-model' produced no output within 5s. (FALLBACK_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT -- change it on the dashboard under Limits & Resilience -> Deadlines)"},"request_id":"req_940fed4ed466498eb67d20a98e4b6dcd"}
```

Same server restarted with **no override** — the shipped zeros — and the same silent upstream: the request was still open when curl gave up at **40.015 s** (exit 28, http 000, no body). Nothing in MCC ended it, which is the promise.

**Invariants held green and named:** `tests/providers/test_credential_rotation.py`, `tests/providers/test_rotation_preemption.py`, `tests/providers/test_stream_recovery.py`, `tests/application/test_execution.py`, `tests/application/test_route_health.py` — 244 passed, including the #216 rotation contracts, the #209 stream-recovery contracts and the #214 preemption contracts.

**New tests:** `tests/application/test_deadline_hints.py` (20), `tests/contracts/test_deadline_hint_labels.py` (5), `tests/api/test_deadline_hint_reaches_the_client.py` (3, real `/v1/messages` streaming and non-streaming through the redaction pass), plus deadline-default pins in `tests/config/test_limit_bounds.py` and three jsdom assertions for the calculator's all-zero state and the `N × floor > total` boundary at six versus three models.

`uv run pytest -q` → **7,835 passed, 15 failed, 38 skipped** — exactly the known **15**-failure baseline (8 websearch reading a real `~/.fcc/.env` key, 6 `test_install_ps1_*`, `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`). jsdom 123 (node 24). `ruff format` / `ruff check` / `ty check` clean repo-wide. Version bumped 6.15.0 → 6.16.0 with `uv lock` in the same commit.

## Residual risks

- **The zeros are the whole risk, and they are the point.** A misbehaving upstream that accepts a request and never speaks now holds it until `HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT` (300 s, applied per read) or the client disconnects. Anyone who wants the old behaviour sets the three keys; anyone upgrading who already set them is unaffected.
- The share-floor arithmetic and its calculator warnings are now dormant by default, so they are exercised only by tests until an operator sets a total budget. The jsdom suite drives both states.
- `fallback_reasoning_answer_timeout` has no `LIMIT_RANGES` entry, so it never joined the blank-coercion validator: clearing that box on the dashboard writes `KEY=` and fails validation at startup. **Pre-existing and unchanged** — equally true when it shipped at 450 — and pinned by a test that says so rather than skipping silently.

## Not done

- **`FALLBACK_HONOUR_CLIENT_TIMEOUT`** (honour the client's `x-stainless-timeout` as the total budget when the budget is 0) is deliberately left out. It cannot be built without touching the deadline path in `execution.py`, which this change is explicitly scoped out of, and it is well past the ~40-line budget it was offered under. The docs describe the zeros honestly instead, which was the non-negotiable half.
- **`.env.example` still quotes 180/600/450.** Reads and edits of that path are denied to agents in this environment; the attempt was made and refused, and not routed around. The manifest, README and USAGE carry the real defaults. One manual edit.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01RnTQRD2QEyAEcEPPahbZu6

feat(deadlines): ship every deadline at 0, and name the knob in the error

180s killed models that were doing real work. The five deadline defaults
(180s first token, 600s total budget, 180s share floor, 180s stall, 450s
thinking) were measured off 21 days of this project's own traffic and were
right for that traffic; they were wrong for a reasoning model that
legitimately thinks for half an hour, and the failure they produced was the
expensive one. The reader was then told "Provider 'x' produced only reasoning
for 450s without answering." -- true, and useless: nothing in that sentence
says which of eleven settings did it, or where the box lives.

Mechanism. `RouteExecutionPolicy` reads its five limits from
`config/constants.py`; every `> 0` guard in `_chunk_timeout` and
`_attempt_deadline` already treats 0 as "disabled", and `LIMIT_RANGES` already
admits 0 for each of them, so a zero default needs no code path of its own.
The messages are all built in one place, `_timeout_failure`, which is also
what the committed-stream truncation path records on the attempt row -- so a
hint appended there travels every route the message takes.

  ends a silent or stalled upstream on its own; the fallback chain moves only
  on an error the provider returns. That is the deliberate product position
  (this is a server its operator configures), and it is now stated in one
  place each in the README, docs/USAGE.md, the Deadlines card blurb and the
  in-dashboard Guide, together with what each limit measures and how to get
  time-based failover back. An install that already sets any of the five keys
  keeps its own value.
* New `application/deadline_hints.py`: `limit_hint(env_var)` appends
  ` (<ENV_VAR> -- change it on the dashboard under Limits & Resilience ->
  <Card>)` to the message. The card label is read out of the admin manifest's
  own `SECTIONS`, and a contract test pins the page name against the nav label
  in `admin.js`, so the words cannot drift from the page they point at.
  Applied at the five deadline messages, the stepped-over cooldown verdict,
  and the one "All API keys for this provider are in cooldown" string in
  `providers/runtime/rotating.py`. The hint names the limit that *actually*
  ended the attempt: a silent model cut short by its slice of the request
  budget names `FALLBACK_ATTEMPT_SHARE_FLOOR`, not the first-token box that
  never fired. ASCII throughout, because this text crosses an SSE frame, a
  JSON body, a log row and a terminal.
* Manifest defaults and prose move with the constants (the constants<->
  manifest guard passes with no exemption added), and the Deadlines
  calculator's all-zero state is now pinned: every route reads "no limit" and
  no budget warning fires, because there is no budget.

No deadline, retry, rotation or fallback logic changed. `_timeout_env_var`
reads the decision `_deadline_reached` already made; `share_bound` is a
boolean that picks a string.

Verification.

Real executor, shipped policy, four silent fake models: the request is still
running after 1.5s and only the first model was ever reached
(test_the_shipped_policy_never_ends_a_silent_model_itself). One knob set and
the chain walks all four and ends with the hint.

Live, isolated server on 127.0.0.1:8199 with HOME/USERPROFILE redirected to a
scratch home (8082 and ~/.fcc untouched), against a local upstream that
accepts the request and then produces nothing. With
FALLBACK_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT=5, both streaming and non-streaming return HTTP
504 and this body:

  {"type":"error","error":{"type":"timeout_error","message":"Provider
  'custom_fake/fake-model' produced no output within 5s.
  (FALLBACK_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT -- change it on the dashboard under Limits &
  Resilience -> Deadlines)"},"request_id":"req_940fed4ed466498eb67d20a98e4b6dcd"}

Same server restarted with no override -- the shipped zeros -- and the same
silent upstream: the request was still open when curl gave up at 40.015s
(exit 28, http 000, no body). Nothing in MCC ended it, which is the promise.

pytest 7,850 passed with the known 15-failure baseline (8 websearch reading a
real key, 6 test_install_ps1_*, test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_
and_direct_cache); jsdom 123; ruff format / ruff check / ty clean repo-wide.

Not done.

* `FALLBACK_HONOUR_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` (honour the client's `x-stainless-timeout`
  as the total budget when the budget is 0) is deliberately left out. It
  cannot be built without touching the deadline path in `execution.py`, which
  this change is scoped out of, and it is well past the ~40-line budget it was
  offered under. The docs describe the zeros honestly instead.
